action_items: Samira: Share tracer + request-logs quickstart and demo recording (due 2027-01-25)
Marta: Confirm compliance checklist items and questions for Redwood (due 2027-01-29)
Ethan: Provide sample traffic patterns and failure cases for pilot (due 2027-01-28)
summary: AE + SE walkthrough of Redwood Console focusing on tracing, error analysis, and request logs. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated for inference; main concerns are latency variability, PII/data residency, and auditability. Agreed to run a pilot benchmark and share security docs.
transcript:
00:00 Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan with Redwood, and Samira our solutions engineer is here. Quick intro round?
00:10 Ethan (Atlas): Hi, Ethan Ross, lead ML eng at Atlas Health. We've got Priya, Marta, Alex on — thanks for doing this.
00:18 Priya (Atlas): Priya Desai, Director of Eng. We're mostly interested in debugging flows and auditability for clinical workflows.
00:25 Samira (Redwood SE): Great. Today we'll walk through Console tracing, error analysis, and request logs — how they help debugging and SLA investigations. We'll also show how to link traces back to raw request payloads securely.
00:40 Jordan (Redwood AE): Before we jump in, quick qual: what's your current inference setup and traffic profile?
00:50 Ethan (Atlas): We're running a mix — some hosted LLMs via a provider, some in-house on GCP VMs. Peak is ~120 reqs/s for our triage model, average 20ms to 400ms latency depending on batch and model. We care about tail latency and reproducibility when a prompt returns junk.
01:10 Alex (Atlas SRE): Also we need audit logs for every model call, retention for 12 months, and SSO integration. We have an internal KMS.
01:20 Samira: That maps to features we typically show. I'll pull up the Console — pardon the small hiccup, my screen share is lagging. (murmur) — okay switching to the tracing tab.
01:40 Samira: So here is the request list, you can filter by route, model, status, and time window. Notice the column for trace_id which ties into the distributed trace. If you click a trace, we open a waterfall view showing per-stage times: routing, queueing, model inference, KV-cache lookup, and network.
02:05 Marta (Atlas Security): When you say KV-cache, do you mean KV cache? Is any of the cache persisted outside our VPC?
02:12 Samira: Good callout. For Redwood Dedicated and Private, caching respects your network boundaries. For hosted, we default to tenant-isolated caches; we can provide a config to avoid cross-tenant caching. I'll note that in the security notes.
02:30 Jordan: Also worth saying how we tag traces — you can include request metadata like customer_id, environment, but we mask PII by default unless you opt-into richer logging. Marta, I think that helps the compliance angle.
02:50 Marta: Yes, but we need to see the specific masking policies and where encryption is applied at rest and in transit.
03:00 Jordan: We'll share the SOC 2 and encryption docs after this call.
03:10 Samira: Back to the example: here's a trace for a failing request. See the big spike in the model inference stage — that's a 1.2s outlier. The Console links the request to the raw request log, you can see prompt payload (redacted fields) and the response body.
03:35 Ethan: That raw request view — can we download or export it for offline analysis?
03:40 Samira: Yes, you can export CSV or JSON for selected traces; for sensitive fields those are masked unless you've configured redaction differently. There's an option to stream logs to your SIEM via our log forwarder or ship to S3 (Private/Dedicated customers often use our forwarder).
04:00 Alex: For the pilot we prefer forwarding to our S3 with server-side encryption and then we run our own analytics. Can the forwarder be configured to only push error-level logs?
04:12 Samira: Yes, we can filter by status, latency thresholds, or custom tags.
04:20 Samira: Now the error analysis panel — we surface errors by type, top routes by error rate, and correlated traces. You can click a cluster of similar errors and see sample request snapshots and the stack of middleware that's invoked.
04:45 Priya: Do you keep request headers? We need to ensure Authorization headers are never stored.
04:52 Samira: We scrub auth headers by default; other headers are optional and can be toggled.
05:00 Jordan: Let's talk routing and fallbacks briefly — if a model variant is overloaded, requests can be routed to a cheaper compatible model. That shows up in the trace as a different model name with a fallback tag.
05:15 Ethan: How do you define compatibility? We have custom prompt templates and constraints around hallucinations.
05:22 Samira: Compatibility is based on model architecture and a mapping you control; we also recommend a small eval set to validate outputs. Redwood Optimize can give recommendations on quantization and model variants per route.
05:40 Marta: We'll need proof that fallbacks won't expose PHI to a different tenant or region.
05:46 Jordan: For Dedicated/Private we keep everything in your tenancy; fallbacks can be configured only among variants you approve.
06:00 Samira: Okay, jumping to request logs debugging flow: you can open a single request and attach a trace, replay the request in a sandboxed runner (no external calls), and see token-level timing.
06:20 Ethan: Replay is huge for us. Does replay re-run against the exact model snapshot?
06:25 Samira: Yes — when we retain the model version and KV-cache snapshot. Note for hosted we retain snapshots for a configurable window; for Dedicated you can pin versions longer.
06:40 Jordan: Quick note on telemetry sampling — to keep costs down we sample at 1% by default for traces, but you can increase sampling per route during a pilot.
06:50 Alex: Can we set alerting on an increase in tail latency that automatically increases trace sampling?
06:56 Samira: Yep, you can set rules: threshold -> increase sampling -> run a diagnostic job. We'll demo that in the pilot.
07:10 (short pause, typing sounds)
07:25 Samira: I'm opening the anomaly explorer: you can see an uptick on route /triage/v1 at 10:40 AM yesterday. If we click into the group, we can see top correlated features — a particular token pattern and one backend host.
07:45 Ethan: That host is our suspicion — we get GC pauses sometimes. Can I annotate traces with our internal host id?
07:52 Samira: Yes, you can add custom tags; we advise sending hashed host ids to avoid PII.
08:00 Ethan: How long are traces retained? We need 90 days for debugging, 12 months for audit logs.
08:08 Samira: Traces: configurable 7–90 days by default; request logs/audit exports can be retained externally for 12 months via S3 or your preferred storage for Dedicated/Private.
08:20 Marta: About SSO and RBAC — we need role separation so devs can't access full raw payloads.
08:26 Jordan: RBAC is supported; you can create roles that exclude 'raw_request_view' and restrict access to only aggregated metrics. We'll include that in the security pack.
08:40 (crosstalk)
09:00 Priya: On the performance side: last time we tried a managed provider we saw 2x cost for the same latency. How does Redwood help with cost?
09:10 Jordan: A few levers: batching controls, prefix/KV caching, quantization recommendations, and choosing model variants. Our Optimize module can run a cost-vs-quality sweep and suggest settings.
09:25 Ethan: Can Optimize tie changes to a canary rollout? We want to A/B compare outputs.
09:30 Samira: Yes — Console supports canary rollouts; you can route a percentage of traffic to variant B and capture eval metrics on the fly.
09:40 Priya: What about encryption at rest for logs and traces?
09:44 Jordan: We encrypt in transit and at rest; you can bring your own KMS for Dedicated/Private. We'll send details.
10:00 Samira: I'll show the request-logs query language — it's SQL-like, you can filter by trace_id, response_code, latency > 500, and then join with your custom metadata tags.
10:20 (screen scroll)
10:30 Samira: Here's an example query: SELECT trace_id, route, latency_ms FROM requests WHERE latency_ms > 500 AND model = 'redwood-trio-v1' ORDER BY latency_ms DESC; you can pin that as an alert.
10:50 Ethan: The model name is a bit different from our internal naming — any mapping control?
10:55 Samira: You can map internal model aliases to Redwood model IDs in the route config.
11:10 Jordan: Let's cover the pilot scope: 1) Send security pack + pricing 2) Customer provides sample traffic and failure cases 3) Redwood runs a 48h benchmark and increases trace sampling on target routes 4) Review results and a short tech deep-dive.
11:30 Priya: That sounds good. Timeline — we want results before end of Feb to decide for Q1 procurement.
11:40 Jordan: We can aim for pilot in the week of Jan 31 and deliver initial results by Feb 2.
11:50 Samira: Quick note — when you run the pilot, we'll show how request logs and traces correlate so you can diagnose root cause quickly. Also, we can forward logs to your S3 bucket.
12:05 Marta: One last security question: do you provide an attestation around data residency? We can't have logs leave EU region for EU customers.
12:12 Jordan: For Private/Dedicated we can guarantee region residency; hosted has region-specific deployments — we'll capture specifics in the security doc.
12:25 (typing)
12:40 Ethan: Thanks, this was helpful. We'll get the sample traffic and confirm dates.
12:50 Jordan: Great, we'll send the pricing and SOC2 pack and record a short demo clip of the tracing flows. Any other questions?
13:00 Priya: None from me.
13:05 Marta: No.
13:08 Jordan: Perfect. Recap of next steps: Jordan sends pricing + security pack, Samira shares the recording and quickstart, Atlas provides traffic and failure cases, and we schedule pilot.
13:25 (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings ("KV cash"/"KV cache"), informal speech preserved, some speaker labels generic; timestamps approximate.
